introduction: When the fifth-generation Sprinter range moved to front-wheel drive in 1983, Toyota kept its sporty Trueno coupés on a rear-drive platform. The GT-APEX 3-door paired pop-up headlamps with the new twin-cam 4A-GE engine, creating a light, balanced car that later became a drifting icon.

drawings.label: Toyota Sprinter Trueno AE86, side elevation

chassis.label: Rear suspension
chassis.value: Four-link live axle with lateral rod and coil springs

entries.title: Launched as a rear-drive holdout
entries.detail: Toyota released the fifth-generation Sprinter on 12 May 1983. While the sedans switched to front-wheel drive, the Trueno coupés stayed rear-wheel drive and were set apart from the sister Corolla Levin by retractable headlamps.

entries.title: Replaced by front-drive successor
entries.detail: AE86 production ended in 1987, when the next Sprinter Trueno (AE92) moved the line to front-wheel drive, leaving the AE86 as the last rear-drive Trueno of its era.

entries.title: Pop-culture fame through Initial D
entries.detail: The manga Initial D, first published in 1995, made a Sprinter Trueno its hero's mountain-pass delivery car, a role widely credited with driving up the car's collector value.
